title: Friends remember Alex Tughan
article: Friends of the late Alex Tughan, 22, are remembering the Oakville man as an amazing snowboarder, a creative skateboarder and someone who was always there to listen when those he cared about needed to talk.
Katie Kittan, who set up a Facebook memorial page for Tughan, said the former White Oaks Secondary School student was the man fatally shot by Halton police on Oak Springs Road Sunday night.
Neither Halton police or Ontario's Special Investigations Unit (SIU) have released the name of the deceased.
"He was a really good person. He was friends with everyone," Kittan, who attended White Oaks with Tughan, told the Oakville Beaver.

"He had some hard times, but he always had a smile on his face and was happy. He was funny, he was a daredevil. If you wanted to know who Alex was you'd find him wearing one of his beanie hats or wearing his hat sideways and holding a skateboard - doing crazy tricks. You'd always see him around the school with his skateboard."
Photos posted by friends on the memorial page feature Tughan at various stages of his life from his teenage years to the recent past.
In some photos, he can be seen flying over snow-covered hills on his snowboard while others show him walking along a beach and smiling while holding his young nephew.
Kittan said she lost touch with Tughan after high school, but caught up with him in September.
"He was doing pretty good. He told me he had been working full time," said Kittan.

"When I talked to him last, he was telling me he was going to possibly join the army so he could save up and move out West. He said he wanted to open his own snowboard shop. He told me that was his dream."
Tughan's snowboarding and skateboarding adventures were widely discussed by those who posted on his memorial page.
Others remembered jumping off the roofs of houses into pools with Tughan much to the chagrin of his parents.
Still others remembered how Tughan went above and beyond for those he cared about.
"I will always remember the way you were able to make me smile and laugh when I was down, even when you weren't always happy," reads a post by Jackie LaFace.

"You always made it your goal to make those around you happy. I'll remember the times all of us had hanging around your pool or just adventuring around Oakville because what else were 13-14 year olds going to do?"
Kittan described Tughan as a truly straightforward and genuine person, who did not select his friends, but was simply friends with everyone.
Another writer on the Facebook page lamented the loss.
"Had a lot of good times. I still can't believe it," posted Stefano Michael Roaro.

The SIU, which is investigating the Sunday shooting, said at 10:45 p.m. Halton police received a call that led them to a residence on Oak Springs Road. There the officers found a man seated in a vehicle a few houses away from the residence.
Monica Hudson of SIU Communications said preliminary information indicates the man got out of the vehicle and there was an 'interaction' that resulted in officers discharging their firearms.
The man was struck down and pronounced dead shortly after midnight.
A, eye witness said the man appeared to be armed with gun.
Kittan, like many who posted to the memorial page, is in a state of disbelief over Tughan's death.
"I was pretty shocked. I'm still shocked," she said. "I didn't think something like that could happen."
As of early Wednesday, Tughan's memorial page had nearly 200 members.
"He deserves to be remembered," said Kittan, regarding her motivation for setting up the page.
"People deserve to see photos of him and hear the funny memories."
Alex Tughan, according to the website www.artway.eu, was the son of Canadian artist James Tughan and social worker Donna Kaufman.
